title: Bexleyheath Emergency Help Points
summary: Emergency medical services, urgent treatment centres, and hazard guidance for Bexleyheath, DA6, and DA7.
content:
Life-threatening emergencies are always 999 first. For urgent clinical advice when lines are up, dial NHS 111.

1. Nearest 24-Hour A&E Hospitals:
- Queen Elizabeth Hospital, Stadium Road, Woolwich SE18 4QH. From Bexleyheath station: ~5 miles west; take bus 89 or 486 west via Shooters Hill Road (~30 min ride).
- Darent Valley Hospital, Darenth Wood Road, Dartford DA2 8DA. From Bexleyheath clock tower: ~6 miles east via A2206/A2; take bus 96 eastbound directly to the hospital (~35 min ride).
- King's College Hospital, Denmark Hill, Camberwell SE5 9RS (Nearest Major Trauma Centre).

2. Urgent Treatment Centres:
- Erith Urgent Treatment Centre, Erith Hospital, Park Crescent, Erith DA8 3EE. Open daily 08:00–20:00. From Bexleyheath Market Place: ~2.5 miles northeast; take bus 229 or B12 (~20 min ride).
- Queen Mary's Urgent Treatment Centre, Queen Mary's Hospital, Frognal Avenue, Sidcup DA14 6LT. Open 24/7. From Bexleyheath station: ~3 miles south; take bus 269 or B14 (~20 min ride).

3. Local Hazards & Flood Risks:
- The River Shuttle flows west-to-east along the southern boundary of Bexleyheath towards the River Cray, creating surface and fluvial flood hazards across Danson Park and adjacent valley roads.
- The A2 corridor running south of the town centre can present major traffic barriers during evacuations.

4. Supplies & Essentials:
- Supermarkets and high-street chemists along Broadway Bexleyheath, Market Place, and Graham Road supply water, first-aid kits, and essential medicines during prolonged utility cuts.

Note: addresses and opening hours may have changed — confirm on arrival where possible.
